title: Reconnect splay, per-session idle-extension, and speculative toolcall guard for streaming
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: we see production flaps where clients concurrently reconnect en masse (region failovers, mobile flurries) causing thundering reconnect bursts that manifest as transient toolcall duplication, frequent session eviction, and tail latency spikes. Motivation: reduce client reconnection storms, avoid accidental duplicate tool invocations when clients reconnect and retry, and allow short client-side pauses (mobile backgrounding) without immediate session eviction. This PR introduces three coordinated mechanisms: 1) reconnect splay: the server returns a randomized reconnect-backoff-splay window in the reconnect-accept payload and the client SDK is instructed to apply jitter prior to reconnect attempts; server-side admission respects splay windows to evenly smooth reconnect bursts across backends; 2) per-session idle-extension: sessions now carry an idle-extension token with a default grace window (configurable per-customer) that can be dynamically extended by authenticated heartbeats from the client or SDK during short backgrounding; server TTL eviction checks consider the extension token so short pauses do not force replays; 3) speculative toolcall guard: when a reconnecting client indicates it is resuming an in-flight streaming session, the server marks recent toolcall intents as speculative and routes tool calls through an idempotency fence which requires a client-sent resume-proof to commit a speculative toolcall. Without a proof the speculative call is rolled back or retried safely. Implementation summary: - Protocol: updated resume handshake includes splay_window_ms and optional resume_proof header; client SDKs get backward-compatible behavior (old clients default to 0ms splay and no resume_proof, speculative guard is conservative). - Server: admission controller implements splay smoothing across replicas, session store tracks idle_extension_until and speculative_toolcall table with commit/abort state and short retention. - Tooling: new tracing spans and metrics (stream.reconnect.splay.ms, stream.session.idle_extension.count, stream.toolcall.speculative.*) and dashboards updated. - Backwards compatibility: safe defaults ensure no regression for older clients. - Testing: end-to-end system tests simulate mass reconnects, unit tests for idempotency fence, fuzz tests for resume_proof mismatches. Rollout plan: staged feature-flagged rollout to 10% customers for 48h with observability alerts on increased speculative-toolcall abort rates, then 50% for 72h before global enable. Linear tasks referenced in linked_linear. This PR also includes VS code SDK hints and notes for SDK teams to update resume behavior.
